items.title: Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: We had Bud Scott, Papa Mutt, Eddie Garland, myself, Ory, and I think we had Fred Washington for a while.

ctx.x: That Taxi Dance Hall, was that on 3rd Street?

Yeah, 3rd, right off of Maine. There was two we worked. We worked one there and one at a fellow by the name of Jack Goldboy. See, he had one. It's called Red Mill. So we worked this Taxi Dance Hall until Ory got lined up pretty good, and that's when we changed the band a little around. Then we had the real band we had. We had Bud Scott, Papa Mutt, Eddie Garland, myself, Ory, and I think we had Fred Washington for a while.
We saw Fred Washington last night.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: We had Minor Hall on drums

ctx.x: David Jones playing alto, mellophone and sax. We had Johnny Dots playing clarinet. We had Lilian Armstrong on piano. We had Minor Hall on drums, and we had Notre Dutre on trombone, and myself on bass, and King Oliver was playing. That's the way the band was picked up when we went to Frisco, playing at the Procola dance hall.
And when you came west, did you plan to stay here, or did you just come for a short trip? Well, we come to play that engagement, that's all.

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: If I have to say it myself, there ain't me and Rom nobody like round, which is Minor Mina Hall, [went] together on that, couldn't be beat.

ctx.x: If I have to say it myself, there ain't me and Rom nobody like round, which is Minor Mina Hall, [went] together on that, couldn't be beat. It was -- that Ram was really a rhythm man. On the drums.

That's great. Okay, so, then we spoke about the kind of feeling that the -- the New Orleans rhythm section got, and we spoke a little bit about some of the most important things in jazz bass playing. Now I've heard you play. I heard you play recently.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: And I was on the bass. Ram was on the drums.

ctx.x: They fired Jimmy Polar. Oh yeah. I remember that. You see, I'll give you the lineup of the band we left fairly well with. We had, uh, we think from the piano. We had Lil Hardin on piano. We had Johnny Dotson on Clionet. Joe Oliver on trumpet. Nora Dutre on trombone. Uh, we had, uh, Jimmy Polar on violin. Uh, we had a band. And I was on the bass. Ram was on the drums. Okay. Then, they want to turn this boy loose, give him a note. Didn't give him no notice. Just fired him.
